Balan K.B vs United India Insurance Company Ltd on 10 June, 2025

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioners in O.P.(MV) No.382/2017 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, North Paravur, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 18/12/2018.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, North Paravur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The sole respondent herein is the third respondent in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioners, on 04/01/2017 at 08:15 p.m. while the deceased was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KL42/G241 along the Vypin- 2025:KER:40491 MACA NO. 469 OF 2020 Munambam road, motorcycle bearing registration no.KL64/A5698 ridden by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner collided with his motorcycle, as a result of which the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Though the deceased was immediately taken to the hospital, he succumbed to the injuries sustained.
A sum of 40,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/owner and the second respondent/rider remained ex parte.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
It was contended that the incident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased.
The age, occupation and income of the deceased were disputed.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A8 were marked on the side of 2025:KER:40491 MACA NO. 469 OF 2020 the claim petitioners.
No documentary evidence was adduced by the third respondent/insurer.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent/rider of the motorcycle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 18,22,300/- together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioners have come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

sentences.text: The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads are challenged by the claim petitioners - Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim 2025:KER:40491 MACA NO. 469 OF 2020 petitioners that the deceased was a driver earning 20,000/- per month.
In order to substantiate the same, Ext.A7 driving licence was produced.
However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 10,000/- only, which is on the lower side.

The learned counsel also draws my attention to the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Allian. Co. Ltd, (2011)
13 SCC 236, as per which the notional income of even a coolie was liable to be fixed at 11,000/- and hence it needs to be appropriately enhanced.
Ext.A7 is the driving licence of the deceased.

sentences.text: The fact that the deceased was a driver is not disputed by the third respondent/insurer.
That being the position, I find that the notional income can be fixed at 12,000/- per month.

Loss of filial consortium Going by the dictums in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram, (2018) 18 SCC 130: 2018 KHC 6697, United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur, AIR 2020 SC 3076: 2023 KHC 760 and New 2025:KER:40491 MACA NO. 469 OF 2020 India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Somwati, 2020 KHC 6530 : (2020) 9 SCC 644, the claim petitioners, who are admittedly the parents of the deceased, are entitled to compensation towards loss of filial consortium at the rate of 40,000/-
each.

Hence, in the light of the aforesaid dictums, loss of filial consortium of 40,000/- each is granted to the claim petitioners.

As per the dictum in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi, 2017 (5) KHC 350: (2017) 16 SCC 680, pronounced on 31/10/2017, the consortium amount has to be enhanced every three years by 10%.
